subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finservcorp.com>, Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan

Hi Alex / Patricia —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the demo. Quick recap and a proposed 4-week POC plan so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners.

Demo recap (high level):
- We covered the inference flow for document ingestion, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for policy summarization, and end-to-end latency profiles for 1–5 concurrent users.
- Live demo used the 7B open model variant, running on our dedicated inference pool with quantization enabled; observed median token latency ~60ms.

Proposed POC goal: validate that Redwood can reliably serve FinServCorp documents with acceptable accuracy and production latency at target throughput while preserving data controls.

Success criteria (please confirm):
1) Accuracy: Top-1 answer precision >= 85% on your internal evaluation set for policy extraction tasks.
2) Latency: P95 per-token latency <= 120ms at your expected peak concurrent sessions (TBD).
3) Reliability: >= 99% availability during business hours for the test window.
4) Security: data stored and processed under your required encryption/KMS controls; audit logs accessible to your team.

POC plan (4 weeks) — quick outline and owners:
Week 0 (kickoff / scope) — Marissa (Redwood): confirm dataset & success metrics, finalize NDA/SOW.
Week 1 (ingest + baseline) — Rishi (Redwood) + FinServ infra: ingest sample dataset (up to 100k docs), run baseline evaluation with 7B model.
Week 2 (tuning + config) — Rishi: test batching/quantization profiles, enable prefix caching, tune prompts.
Week 3 (throughput & reliability) — Rishi + Naomi: run load tests to target concurrent sessions; collect latency/cost metrics.
Week 4 (evaluation & handoff) — Marissa + Naomi: review results, capture runbook, and recommend next steps (Dedicated vs Hosted).

Open items / asks from FinServCorp:
- Confirm the evaluation dataset and how we’ll share sample records (SFTP or secure bucket).
- Approve the proposed success criteria or suggest modifications.
- Confirm target concurrent sessions and any business-hour windows for heavy testing.

Attachments: FinServCorp_POC-outline.pdf (detailed plan) and Demo_Slides.pdf
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the dataset sharing approach and success criteria by EOD Monday 6/21.
2) If approved, we’ll schedule a kickoff call (30–45m) for Tues 6/22 or Wed 6/23 — please send preferred time slots.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0124

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. Quick replies inline.

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 1:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference> wrote:
> (see full message above)

We’re generally aligned on the success criteria. A few clarifications:
- Accuracy: 85% top-1 is acceptable as a starting point; we’ll provide a seeded evaluation set of ~2k labelled examples.
- Latency: our initial target is P95 <= 150ms; if you can hit 120ms that’s great, but we need to be realistic for our 3–5 concurrent analyst workflows.
- Reliability: 99% BH uptime is fine.

On data sharing: procurement needs a security attachment and SOW before we can provision an S3 endpoint to Redwood. I’ll loop in procurement (cc’d Patricia) to start that flow. Patricia — can you share the vendor questionnaire and expected timelines?

Also we’ll need a rough cost estimate for a 4-week trial (hosted consumption) vs a temporary dedicated pool so finance can greenlight. Can you provide a ballpark by EOD Friday?

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

—Alex
